steps.path: The Office page, the file-viewer editor, and the files Office can open
steps.headline: This is what done means for Office — the app's document, spreadsheet and presentation editor.

rows.statement: Office is built on the Euro-Office editors, not the original OnlyOffice ones with its logo rule.
Office ships inside the YouCoded installer as a separate program, with its licence notices and a code link included.
Office ships about 25 common look-alike fonts, plus whatever fonts are already installed on your computer.
Office lives at the top of your Pages list; pinning it uses one of your four pinned-page spots, like any other page.
Office's start screen offers new blank files, your recent Office documents, and this project's other Office files.
On a new install, Office's start screen says your files will appear here instead of showing an empty Recent list.
Several open Office documents appear as tabs across the top of one Office page.
A document tab left idle for a while sleeps to save memory, shown dimmed with a moon, and wakes back where you left it.
Spreadsheet and presentation tabs get your theme around the editor, keep the sheet or slide itself neutral, and switch instantly when awake.
Office saves your work automatically and keeps earlier versions you can restore from a Versions window.
Every version from the last day is kept, then daily for 30 days, capped at 50 versions per file and 1 GB total.
rows.measured: 24h: every version; then 1/day for 30 days; cap 50/file, 1GB total

rows.statement: OnlyOffice's own Version History menu inside the editor is hidden; Office's Versions button is the only place to see and restore versions.
Office saves your changes to the real file automatically, without needing you to press Save.
The small editor inside the file viewer uses YouCoded's own slim toolbar, not OnlyOffice's ribbon.
Opening an Office file in the file viewer shows an instant preview first; editing starts only after you press Edit.
Pressing Edit on a Word, Excel or PowerPoint file swaps the preview for the real editor; there is no Save or Cancel, only Done.
The file panel's header shows an Office briefcase icon instead of open-in-default-app, and the document zooms so its text fills the panel's width.
rows.threshold: ≥65% zoom in the default panel width
rows.measured: 51% → 65% zoom in the default panel width

rows.statement: In the file viewer, the editor's scroll bars and the gap above the page are gone; the document fills the panel edge to edge.
The Edit button on an Office file stays hidden while the session-files list is open, same as it works today.
Pressing Escape while a document is open closes any open editor menu first; with none open, it goes back to chat.
Office edits Word, Excel and PowerPoint files (.docx, .xlsx, .pptx).
Office opens old .doc, .xls and .ppt files; saving converts them to the modern format, after asking first.
LibreOffice .odt, .ods and .odp files open in the first version; editing one saves your changes to a Word, Excel or PowerPoint copy beside it.
rows.note: Amended 2026-09-28 by office-odf#Q-odf-save: the translator turns partly-bold bullet lines fully bold when writing LibreOffice files (found in the spike), so the original is never rewritten.

rows.statement: Office edits CSV tables and warns before saving if something added, such as colours or formulas, cannot be kept in CSV.
Office's editor takes on your theme's colours, font and glass effects, so wallpaper themes stay beautiful behind it.
Office's editor also matches your theme's roundness — buttons, menus, fields and dialogs use your corner-size setting.
This version of Office adds nothing to the assistant: it neither sees nor edits a document you have open.
Office reaches desktop first; on phones, Office files stay preview-only until a later version.
The first testable version of Office includes the Office page and tabs: start screen, open, edit, save.
The first testable version of Office already matches your theme, not OnlyOffice's default look.
Opening Office, opening a Recent file, switching tabs, opening Versions, and editing a file from a conversation all work in a dev instance.
rows.threshold: the described click-through completes without error, in a dev instance
